text: I have never seen a worse paper in my life, for it is one of those sprawling, flamboyant patterns that commit every artistic sin. <break time="0.8s" /> Its lame, uncertain curves, when you follow them for a little distance, suddenly plunge off at outrageous angles and destroy themselves in unheard of contradictions. <break time="0.8s" /> The color is repellent, almost revolting, a smouldering, unclean yellow, strangely faded by the slow turning sunlight, and in some places the paper has been stripped off in great patches. <break time="0.8s" /> John is very careful and loving, and he hardly lets me stir without special direction, for he has a schedule prescription for each hour in the day. <break time="0.8s" /> I feel basely ungrateful not to value his care more, yet John does not know how much I really suffer, for he knows there is no reason to suffer. <break time="0.8s" /> It is fortunate that Mary is so good with the baby, such a dear baby, and yet I cannot be with him myself, for it makes me so nervous. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked John to repaper the room, he said that if he gave in, the heavy bed would come next, then the barred windows, and then the gate at the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> His sister Jennie, a perfect and enthusiastic housekeeper who hopes for no better profession, keeps the house for us and thinks it is the writing which made me sick. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile, the paper stares at me as if it knew what a vicious influence it had, with two bulbous eyes that look at me upside down.
